title: Migration comment still claims tokens are minted lazily at continue-link time; the W1 fix mints them at save
evidence:
Migration comment: "-- continue_token is 288 bits of URL-safe entropy (wisp.random_string(48)),
-- same capability model as application.erasure_token: the token IS the
-- auth. Partial unique index — most rows have NULL (token minted lazily on
-- the first \"email me a link\" request)." — but server/src/application/sql/upsert_application_draft.sql (this chunk) says: "-- continue token is minted at SAVE time (COALESCE keeps an existing one) so
-- every live draft is reachable by the stage-2 reminder's continue-link" and its INSERT is "INSERT INTO application_draft (vacancy_id, email, fields, continue_token)".
detail: Stale design note contradicts the shipped mint-at-save behavior: most rows will have non-NULL tokens, not NULL. Migrations are immutable once merged, so the wrong comment becomes permanent if not fixed pre-merge.
recommended_fix: Reword the comment before merge: token minted at save time (COALESCE preserves an existing one on conflict); the partial unique index guards the negligible collision risk.

title: Spec Suggested Review Order says expiry sweep covers 'closed, archived, or past closes_at' — the W4 fix removed archive from the sweep
evidence:
Spec line 245: "- Expiry sweep phase: closed, archived, or past closes_at." — but server/src/retention/sql/delete_expired_application_drafts.sql (this chunk) says: "-- Archived vacancies keep their drafts: archiving is
-- restorable (AGENTS.md)" and deletes only "WHERE d.vacancy_id = v.id
  AND (
    v.status = 'closed'
    OR (v.closes_at IS NOT NULL AND v.closes_at <= now())
  )".
detail: The same file's change log documents W4 (archive no longer sweeps drafts), yet the Suggested Review Order still describes the pre-fix behavior, misdescribing a GDPR-relevant expiry rule to future reviewers/deployers.
recommended_fix: Update the line to 'Expiry sweep phase: closed or past closes_at (archived vacancies keep drafts — archiving is restorable, W4)'.
